crime.value: Murder of Eddie Larsen by rifle shot during attempted theft; later, murder of Dink O'Day by strangulation. Central question: who killed Eddie Larsen, and why was Jimmy Grover wrongly accused?
crime.quote: Mattick had caught Eddie Larsen in his shed trying to steal some cider and had lit out after him with a rifle. He shot him down and killed him.

victim.value: Eddie Larsen: a drunk man attempting to steal cider from Mattick's shed. Dink O'Day: a man who attempted blackmail after learning of the first murder.
victim.quote: Mattick had caught Eddie Larsen in his shed trying to steal some cider...Dink started getting frisky about it and tried to squeeze a little money out of Mattick

closed_world.value: The small rural town of Capstone and its surrounding farms and woods during wartime (second year of Civil War); social closure: everyone knows everyone.
closed_world.quote: I hadn't ever seen such activity in Capstone. It seemed that everybody was there, all the storekeepers in their aprons and the men from the tavern

culprit_and_motive.value: Jack Mattick: murdered Eddie Larsen to prevent theft from his shed, then murdered Dink O'Day to silence blackmail. Motive: property protection and extortion prevention.
culprit_and_motive.quote: Mattick had caught Eddie Larsen in his shed trying to steal some cider and had lit out after him with a rifle. He shot him down and killed him...Mattick's fierce temper and he had choked Dink to death

resolution.value: Pete and Gascius discover Dink O'Day's body in a barrel at Mattick's farm; they report to the sheriff, who apprehends Mattick. Mattick confesses to both murders. Jimmy Grover is exonerated and receives the reward money.
resolution.quote: The sheriff collared him good and led him off...Mattick tell it in the jail to the sheriff and all the others: Mattick had caught Eddie Larsen in his shed trying to steal some cider and had lit out after him with a rifle.

investigator.value: Pete Mariah and Gascius (the narrator), two teenage boys: amateur investigators driven by curiosity and conscience. They stumble upon evidence through exploration rather than official authority.
investigator.quote: Pete said, 'I'll tell you one thing. They're going to hang him as soon as they let eyes on him.' We went off into the night-webbed trees...and found the dead body in the barrel.
